prospect.name: Chris Valiente
prospect.occupation: Project manager at a managed services provider, running their national installation projects; works from home. Seventeen years military — US Navy, deployed to Afghanistan attached to the Army in 2012 — currently transitioning to civilian life and appealing a medical board decision.
prospect.family_status: Remarried; wife works outside the home and is unhappy with her own fitness. One daughter aged 10, co-parented with his ex-wife. Recently bought a half-million-dollar five-bedroom house. Father is a Cuban immigrant.
prospect.training_background: Peaked at 186 lb, his heaviest, around March last year. Went to physical therapy saying 'I can't live like this, I have to be able to move' and has since lost about 30 lb. Has been plateaued for roughly three months with about 10 lb to go. Recently suspended his gym membership because it had stopped being enjoyable, and now trains at home five days a week — push-ups, pull-ups, an ab roller, a walking pad — plus a daily walk, sometimes with a weight vest. Physical therapy had him doing goblet squats and deadlifts with a kettlebell, which he enjoyed. Found Trevor on TikTok about a year ago and has wanted to start since. Already bought an adjustable kettlebell he now thinks is unsuitable. Eats on a military-conditioned schedule, roughly 7am to 5pm, at about 1,600-1,900 calories.
prospect.medical: Spine fracture, unresolved. Currently fighting a military medical board over the classification, and receiving nerve blockers as an interim measure — in his own words, 'that's dealing with it until we're ready for surgery', so spinal surgery is anticipated rather than complete. His profile makes him non-deployable. Came off a course of physical therapy which permitted bodyweight squats, kettlebell goblet squats and kettlebell deadlifts; he avoids barbell squats in a rack or on a Smith machine entirely because 'it's too easy to overload' and says he knows immediately when his form slips because 'I feel it so much more than I think more normal people would'. Self-discloses as autistic.

signals: In the middle of a serious active health event rather than recovering from a past one — a spine fracture with surgery anticipated, nerve blockers as an interim measure, and a live medical board appeal
Training is explicitly part of fighting it: went to physical therapy saying 'I can't live like this. I have to be able to move. I have to be able to do things'
Motivation is very high and the intent to start is immediate — 'I'm ready to go. I mean, if we could get me started by next Monday'

Divergence from the archetype: price resistance is present rather than absent. Credit score 580-586, a new half-million-dollar mortgage, and a hard stop pending spousal approval. The archetype predicts an easy close; the finances did not permit one.
Distinguished from the_rebuilder because the health event is ongoing and unresolved, not a season he has come out of

goals.text: Lose the last 10 lb after a three-month plateau — framed as an aesthetic bonus rather than the point
Build functional strength that links his muscle groups, rather than isolated machine movements
Train under coaching so he does not injure himself around the spine fracture
Keep up with a 10-year-old daughter who loves hiking, swimming and long days out — not be the dad on the bench at Disney
Have the body to actually enjoy the freedom of civilian life and travel
Fit training into under an hour before the workday, or into a lunch break
Find structure and a purpose in training again — the gym stopped being fun
Eventually bring his wife in and train alongside her

pains.text: Spine fracture with surgery anticipated, managed in the interim with nerve blockers, and an unresolved medical board appeal after 17 years of service
Stalled at a plateau for about three months with 10 lb still to go
The gym stopped being enjoyable regardless of how he changed his split — 'I really just sat on a machine until my arms got tired'
No structure and no purpose in training since leaving the military environment where everything was contained and scheduled
Nobody to share progress with or ask for adjustments — 'I don't have anybody to share my success with or bounce ideas off of'
Life churn delayed him a year: house purchase and move, co-parenting arrangements, a new job and then a new role inside it
Financial pressure — credit score 580-586, a new half-million-dollar mortgage, actively paying down debt
Ate poorly while demoralised about the medical board outcome
His wife stopped training when he did after his injury and is unhappy with her body

objections.raw_quote: But it would be due today for me to sign up today. So I, I'm not going to drop that money without talking to her about it. Because she knew I was doing this. I've been showing her Trevor's videos... So she knew that this was coming, but I don't know that she expected me to pay for it today.
objections.rep_response: Said 'Okay' and waited. When the prospect said his wife would call back in five minutes the rep offered to stay on — 'if it's gonna be only five minutes, I'm still free' — and then filled roughly thirteen minutes with conversation about Afghanistan, Poland, Cuban heritage and travel while the call never came. Not one move of the scripted play was run.

objections.raw_quote: Oh. Okay. Well, what does the payment structure for that look like?... Yes. I just got a mortgage.
objections.rep_response: Went straight to third-party financing — asked about prior Klarna and Affirm use, asked the credit score directly, warned that 580 might be tricky, and sent the Payva link, which came back approved at $650 a month over 12 months. Genuine and effective work, but no isolation question first, and no company payment plan was ever offered as an alternative to financing that adds $1,800 to the cost.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Third-party financing through Payva, approved live on the call at $650 per month for 12 months — a total of $7,800 for the $6,000 six-month programme, so roughly $1,800 in financing cost. The prospect confirmed 'It's 12 months of $650, and that's doable' but the first payment fell due immediately, which is what triggered the spousal consult. He was separately investigating whether he could fund it from a Health Savings Account or reimburse himself from one, which would have allowed a shorter six or nine month plan. No company-side instalment plan was offered.

prospect_financials.detail: Credit score self-reported as '580, 586'. Recently took a mortgage on a half-million-dollar house, up from a three-bedroom one-bathroom home. Heavy prior user of Klarna and Affirm. Paid tomorrow relative to the call. Has savings but wants to avoid touching them. Holds a Health Savings Account with a balance he was trying to route the payment through. Approved by Payva at $650/month over 12 months.

evidence: Financing was approved live and the prospect confirmed affordability: 'I do see the app. I do see the payment plans. It's 12 months of $650, and that's doable.'
Blocked solely on spousal approval: 'I'm not going to drop that money without talking to her about it.'
The wife never called back within the call — 'It's definitely been five minutes. I wonder if her meetings run over.'
Clear commitment to the work itself: 'Yeah, I'm ready to go. I mean, if we could get me started by next Monday, I would love to start before we leave for the beach.'

Concrete next actions owned by the prospect with a deadline: 'I'll reach out to you by 5 if I haven't heard from HR. I definitely should have heard from my wife by 5. So yeah, I'll follow up with you on the WhatsApp.'
Counter-evidence: no payment was taken, no onboarding call was booked, and the only channel agreed is the rep's personal WhatsApp. Trevor's Monday availability was mentioned but nothing was held.
Counter-evidence: the fallback if HSA reimbursement is refused is to pull from household savings, which is precisely the decision requiring his wife's agreement.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to hear back from his employer's HR on whether he can reimburse himself from his HSA, and to speak with his wife, then message the rep on WhatsApp by 5pm the same day. Trevor has Monday availability but nothing was scheduled.

notable.note: The best-qualified prospect in the batch on intent and the worst-handled at the moment of truth. Discovery was genuinely strong — the setter's notes were read back twice, the root cause was chased until the prospect named it himself ('a purpose, really'), and the injury question was specific and useful. Then a textbook spouse-consult objection landed at 00:48:26 with financing already approved, and the rep ran none of the scripted play, instead filling thirteen minutes with war stories while waiting for a call that never came. Two integrity items sit alongside it: a man awaiting spinal surgery and on nerve blockers was sold a six-month loaded kettlebell programme with no clinician clearance sought, and the rep encouraged him to route payment through a Health Savings Account, a tax-advantaged medical account, for a fitness coaching product. This call also confirms the DH setter code as Derek Harris.
